question_text: A 14-year-old Somalian boy is brought to the emergency department by his mother because of a painful penile erection since he woke up 3 hours ago. His family recently emigrated to the United States from a refugee camp, and his past medical history is unknown. He has never had a health check up prior to this visit. On further questioning, his mother reports that the child is often fatigued and sick, and has episodes of joint pain. Examination shows ejection systolic murmurs heard over the precordium. Examination of the genitalia shows an engorged, tumescent penis. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause?
